extracted.intended_audience: users of the Brookings Regulatory Tracker (policy researchers, journalists, analysts, and members of the public interested in federal regulatory actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and background for using the Brookings Center on Regulation and Markets Regulatory Tracker, including what the tracker includes, how rules are selected, how to navigate search and rule detail features, and key aspects of the federal rulemaking process that affect tracked entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curated inclusion (not comprehensive)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker is not comprehensive; it encompasses a curated set of rules that CRM staff deems to be particularly important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tracker focuses on economically or politically significant, controversial, or otherwise newsworthy regulatory events and excludes rules that are arcane, routine, or otherwise uncontroversial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: media attention
rubrics_metrics.description: If staff finds a rule receives coverage from a major news outlet, then we will consider including it in the tracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media coverage is used as a signal of a rule's newsworthiness; such rules are candidates for inclusion subject to staff review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules that are the subject of any new or ongoing litigation may be included in the tracker after a more detailed review of the litigation action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation indicates potential controversy or legal importance and prompts closer staff review before inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: rollback of prior administration rule
rubrics_metrics.description: At the start of Trump’s second term, rules explicitly aimed at repealing or revising regulations passed during the Biden administration are a focus for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracker emphasizes rules that reverse or substantially alter prior-administration policies (rollback/revision activity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: general impact/staff judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rule does not meet the other qualifications but seems as though it will have a particularly strong impact based on staff judgment, then it may be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff discretion is applied to include high-impact rules even absent media coverage, litigation, or rollback status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion: arcane, routine, or uncontroversial rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Reg Tracker excludes rules that are arcane, routine, or otherwise uncontroversial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion helps keep the tracker focused on significant and newsworthy regulatory events rather than every Federal Register entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal rulemaking and notice-and-comment publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Most entries in the Reg Tracker are regulations enacted through the rulemaking process; rules are typically issued through informal rulemaking which involves a public notice of proposed rulemaking and a public comment period, and all proposed rules are published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should expect tracked agency rules to have NPRMs and Federal Register citations; the public comment period is the core participation mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period typical length
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules typically have commentary periods of around 30 to 60 days, with some exceptions for more complex rules or if an agency justifies a different period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment periods can vary; check the Federal Register entry or rule timeline for the exact comment deadline for any tracked rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-rule public involvement (Petition, ANPRM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a rule is proposed, agencies may gather information through unstructured processes, receive a Petition for Rulemaking, or issue an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to solicit public input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-rule activity can be relevant context for tracked entries and may appear in the rule's background or notes sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for reasoned final agency decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must base their reasoning and conclusions behind the final rulemaking on comments, scientific data, expert opinions, and facts accumulated during pre-rule and proposed rule stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the substantive administrative-law expectation that final rules rest on the administrative record; deficiencies here can be grounds for judicial challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date rule and 'good cause' exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA requires that a final rule go into effect at least 30 days after publication unless the agency justifies an immediate effective date by arguing there is 'good cause' that an immediate effective date is in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trackers and users should note whether an agency invoked 'good cause' for immediate effectiveness and the justification provided in the Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review/vacatur grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may evaluate whether a rule is unconstitutional; exceeds the agency’s authority; was issued without adhering to notice-and-comment procedures mandated by the APA or other applicable laws; or is arbitrary, capricious, or represents an abuse of discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court finding on any of these grounds may vacate all or part of a rule and typically remand it to the agency to correct deficiencies; litigation status is a key tracker element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and filter functionality
rubrics_metrics.description: The search bar allows filtering rules by nature of action, policy area (category), and current status, and includes checkboxes to include rules from the first Trump administration or from the Biden administration; a keyword search combs both headers and detail text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can customize views by administration-era, policy area, action type, and full-text keyword searches to find relevant tracked rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule header metadata fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule header shows a nickname for the rule, nature of action (agency rulemaking or other process), relevant policy categories, the sponsoring agency/agencies, current status, and the date the entry was last updated by CRM staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These header fields provide a quick summary and metadata for each tracked rule entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule detail structure and timeline visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Clicking a rule expands to a brief summary and a detailed overview divided into background, impact, litigation, and notes; for agency rulemaking there is a timeline showing proposal, finalization, and effective dates with links to Federal Register pages; timeline color indicates administration party and arrows or Xs indicate progression or blocking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The structured detail and timeline help users understand the rule’s history, effects, litigation posture, and administrative provenance at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related rules chronological grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional related rules are displayed below a rule heading in chronological order, with older rules listed first; typically a rule is modified or superseded by the rule below it, often issued by a subsequent administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chronological related-content feature helps users follow chains of modification, supersession, or rollback across administrations.
